findings.title: Tool results drop the error object, and the three docs disagree on what a tool result carries
findings.claim: No document says the mod's tools return the envelope's `error`. Architecture says a tool returns the envelope's `result` and `meta.next`. A-4 says `JSON.stringify` of `result` and `meta.next`. Contracts says `result` plus `meta.next`, `meta.seq` and warnings. An error envelope has no `result`, so an agent on the plugin's tools never sees the code, retry class, hint or details. `meta.model_requests` with its re-run handle is dropped too.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1227 ('return the envelope's `result` and `meta.next`'); architecture.md:1518 (A-4: 'returns JSON.stringify of the envelope's result and meta.next as one string'); contracts.md:792 ('the envelope's result plus meta.next, meta.seq and warnings'); contracts.md:84-85 (result and error are mutually exclusive Options). DR-21 (decisions.md amended round 1) makes `retry` classes and the re-run handle the agent's recovery path. KICKOFF principle 2: 'Every capability is reachable through stable, typed, documented interfaces, with stable error codes ... tools agents can call'. S14 (tier A): 'an agent can drive S1 and S2 using only the plugin's tools and skills'.
findings.failure_scenario: In the S14 evidence run, an agent calls room_query `ask path cart worker`. The suffix `cart` matches several records, so the engine returns `ambiguous_ref` with `details.candidates`. Following A-4, the handler stringifies `result` (absent) and `meta.next` (null), and the agent gets `{}` or `null`. It can't pick a candidate and either guesses or gives up. The same thing happens to an agent's `stale_write` (no three-way diff, no `after_reread` class, so no informed retry), to `person_required` (no card ID to hand the person), and to a session-backend request (no re-run handle).
findings.proposed_fix: Define one tool-result shape in contracts.md and generate it from the catalogue: `{ok, result | error{code,retry,message,hint,details}, meta{seq,next,truncated,warnings,model_requests}}`, with empty fields omitted. Make A-4, architecture.md:1227 and contracts.md:792 point to that one definition. Add `tools.test.ts::error_envelopes_reach_the_model` over a golden of each error code, and include error goldens in `tool_results_within_budget`.

findings.title: High-entropy redaction runs over the whole tool output and can mangle IDs, hashes and handles
findings.claim: `kernel::redact` masks 'high-entropy strings' on every mod tool output, with no field scope. Planroom's own stable identifiers look high-entropy: edge IDs `e:`+12 hex, uuid v7 event IDs, card IDs, cursors, commit SHAs in evidence, input hashes. If redaction masks them, the handles and pointers that principle 2 relies on stop working on the tool path, which is the path agents use. No test checks that handles survive redaction.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:881 ('kernel::redact runs on every ... mod tool output. It masks ... high-entropy strings'); contracts.md:792 ('as compact JSON, after kernel::redact'); contracts.md:319 (EdgeId 'e:' + 12 hex), 407 (uuid v7), 93 (opaque cursor), 357 (evidence `commit`); architecture.md:1153 ('handles that are exact command invocations'). KICKOFF principle 2: 'stable IDs and pointers to evidence rather than prose'; 'answers come summary-first, with handles to drill down'.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent asks `why storefront orders` through room_query. The reply's handle names `show e:3fa9c01b7d2e` and its evidence names commit `9c1e...`. The entropy filter masks both, so the agent's follow-up `show [REDACTED]` returns not_found. Paging with a masked `meta.next` cursor fails the same way. The CLI path (raw) and the tool path (masked) now give different answers, so `same_output`-style parity and S14's tools-only drive of S1 and S2 break.
findings.proposed_fix: Scope redaction by schema: mark repo-derived free-text fields in the contract (`#[redact]` on `Evidence.contains`, `ContextExcerpt.excerpt`, `Hint.value`, `ErrorObject.details.stderr`, prompt text), and redact only those. Never redact ID, handle, cursor or hash fields. Add `tools.test.ts::handles_round_trip_after_redaction`: every handle in every golden tool result, re-issued, returns ok.

findings.title: Chat proposals need a file on disk, which adds a Write permission prompt to every proposal batch
findings.claim: In chat, the planning partner proposes S3 items 'through room_change', but the only proposal leaves are `intent propose --file F` and `edit propose --file`. The tool input is a list of CLI argument strings, so the model must first write a JSON file with the Write tool. In default mode that's a permission prompt for every batch, and the file lands somewhere unspecified, maybe the person's working tree. The guard blocks `.planroom/`. The curator has no Write tool at all, so it must fall back to Bash heredocs, which prompt as well.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:976 ('it proposes items itself through room_change (ghosts, one batch per turn)'); architecture.md:1138-1139 (`intent ... propose --file F`, `edit ... propose --file`); contracts.md:783 (`args`: array of strings); architecture.md:401 (the guard denies Write under `.planroom/`); architecture.md:1106 and 1231 (curator submits with `edit propose --file`; tools `Read, Bash, Grep, Glob`). DR-22, amended for round-1 principles-7: ghost-only leaves are auto-allowed so a proposal doesn't interrupt twice. KICKOFF principle 1: 'Interrupt a person only for decisions only they can make'; R5 and the S3 evidence path in a live session.
findings.failure_scenario: In the S3 evidence run ('Add retries to the worker' through /room intent), each of six stages makes Claude Write `proposal-outcome.json` and so on. Each Write raises a permission prompt the person must approve before the proposal even exists as a ghost, and then they still review the ghosts. The JSON files are left in the repo working tree. Six extra interruptions per plan, none of them a decision only the person can make.
findings.proposed_fix: Let the proposal travel inline. Add a `payload` object (the `PlanProposal` or edit batch) to the `room_change` input. The mod handler writes it to `.planroom/models/inbox/<tool_use_id>.json` (the mod isn't guarded) and passes `--file` itself. Alternatively accept `--file -` on stdin through `process.run`. Give the curator the same inline path. Add a mod test asserting that an S3 stage proposal produces no Write call and no file outside `.planroom/`.

findings.title: A canvas reload or serve restart strands the tab's pending edits and leaves an undefined screen
findings.claim: Pending canvas edits 'survive a reload in sessionStorage'. But a reloaded tab has no bearer token, and the only way back in is `e` or `/room open`, which opens a new tab. sessionStorage is per tab, so the new tab has none of the old tab's pending edits, and the old tab can't send them. `serve` binds a random port each start and exits after 30 minutes with no client, so after a laptop sleep even localStorage would sit on a dead origin. No document defines what an unauthorized or disconnected tab shows, and the empty-state audit doesn't visit that state.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1256 ('Pending edits survive a reload in sessionStorage ... until confirmed'); architecture.md:1173 ('A reload asks for a new code: e or /room open'); architecture.md:1171-1172 (`open` opens the URL in the browser itself); architecture.md:1158 (binds `127.0.0.1:0`); architecture.md:156 (exits after 30 min with no client); decisions.md:552 ('a reload of the tab asks for a new code, one e press'); architecture.md:1274 (empty_state_audit covers views on an empty workspace, not an auth-lost tab). KICKOFF principle 1: 'Never show a blank state ... Never lose or overwrite what someone did.'
findings.failure_scenario: The person regroups two blocks on the canvas and closes the laptop. Serve sees no client for 30 minutes and exits. On wake, the edit was never acknowledged (or was sent after wake to a dead port) and sits pending in that tab. They press `e`, and a new tab opens on a new port with an empty sessionStorage. The regroup is gone from every surface, while the old tab still draws it as pending, or draws an error. The edit is lost, the screen is inconsistent, and recovery takes a trip to the terminal.
findings.proposed_fix: (a) Have serve prefer the port in the last `serve.json`, so the origin is stable. (b) Keep the canvas outbox in localStorage keyed by workspace_id, with the idem already minted, and replay it in any newly authenticated tab, which is safe because of idempotency. (c) Define an engine-authored `disconnected` and `needs_login` state with one next action ('Press e in Claude Code'), and add it to `empty_state_audit`. (d) Add `e2e: reload_mid_edit_keeps_the_edit` and `serve_restart_keeps_pending_edits`.

findings.title: DR-60 dropped the out-of-tree pack card, but the tier A CI paths still decide it, and the setup card is unaccounted for
findings.claim: DR-60 removed the first-load card for a person-listed out-of-tree pack, on principle-1 grounds. `feature_list.json` (fixture_note, S1 asserts, S7 steps) and DR-48's consequences still depend on that card. The S7 CI path tells the harness to `decide CARD keep` on a card that never exists. The S1 card budget counts it among its 3. Neither path says whether the Jev setup card ('when no backend is configured') is dealt under strict replay with no credential. If it is, it stays open through S7's rescan and uses up TRUTH's `max_cards: 1`. The setup card is also asked per workspace, though its answer (no gateway key) is a user-level fact. DR-60's `Command::PersonInit` is missing from the contracts catalogue, the leaf table and the undo-class table.
findings.evidence: decisions.md:1152-1159 (DR-60: 'A pack that a person lists in config ... loads with no card'); feature_list.json:4 ('the first scan deals its one first-load card (DR-48)'); feature_list.json:42 ('the Ruby pack's first-load card among them'); feature_list.json:365 ('planroom decide CARD keep ... for the Ruby pack's first-load card'); decisions.md:861 (DR-48: 'the Ruby pack's first-load card is dealt on every fixture'); architecture.md:958 and decisions.md:897 (setup card); feature_list.json:1256 ('at most 3 cards plus the one Jev setup card'); TRUTH scenarios.S7.max_cards = 1; contracts.md:217-231 and architecture.md:1118-1123 (no PersonInit). KICKOFF S7 (tier A): 'raises at most one card'; principle 1.
findings.failure_scenario: A track implements DR-60 as written. The S7 CI path's step 5 has no CARD to pick, so the step fails or the harness grabs whatever card is on top, maybe the Jev setup card. If the setup card is dealt under replay and isn't picked, it's still open after the routine rescan, and any regression or other card makes 2, failing `routine_rescan_at_most_one_card`. If a track instead keeps the card to satisfy feature_list, every fixture scan interrupts for a choice the person already made, the exact principle-1 violation DR-60 removed.
findings.proposed_fix: Propagate DR-60. Remove the first-load card from feature_list.json (fixture_note, S1 asserts, S7 step 5) and from DR-48's consequences. State in DR-50 whether strict replay counts as a configured backend (it should, so CI deals no setup card), and add an S7 assert that no setup card is open. Make the Jev setup choice user-level (in DATA_ROOT), not per workspace. Add `person init` to the contracts catalogue, the leaf and actor table and the undo-class table (Query or Compensate).

findings.title: A person-stakes card calls Claude when it reaches the top of the stack, whatever Jev's confidence
findings.claim: DR-50 and the decision loop ask Claude for every person-stakes card when it 'reaches the top of the stack', with no band check, so confident Jev picks pay for Claude too. The Policy bands section says Claude is offered lazily, in the escalate band only. 'Reaching the top' happens on a read (focus refresh, the card closing above it), so a read becomes a paid call, and the docs don't say which process makes it or under which lease and budget. This contradicts R9's three bands and 'cheap decisions go to Jev, not Claude'.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:776 (`card --> card: Claude asked when the card is on top or a person taps Ask Claude`); architecture.md:794 ('the engine asks Claude only when the card reaches the top of the stack or the person taps "Ask Claude"'); decisions.md:898 (same); compare architecture.md:893 ('In the escalate band ... a person card offers "Ask Claude", run lazily'). KICKOFF R9: 'above a measured confidence bar, Planroom acts or pre-fills; in the uncertain band, a one-tap card with Jev's pick pre-selected; beyond that, it escalates to Claude'; principle 2: 'cheap decisions go to Jev, not Claude'.
findings.failure_scenario: A rename orphans 30 overrides, and `override_retarget` deals person cards with confident Jev picks (0.9). As the person taps through them, each new top card sends a capable-tier Claude call, so 30 Claude calls for decisions Jev had already pre-answered, against the daily budget. In S7's live evidence, any person card left open after the routine rescan gets a Claude call when a `focus` refresh puts it on top, which breaks '0 Claude calls on the routine path'.
findings.proposed_fix: Make one rule: a person-stakes card asks Claude only in the escalate band, and only on an explicit 'Ask Claude' tap or when the card is first dealt inside a duty under the `decide` lease and the per-day budget. Never trigger a call from a read. Fix the loop table, DR-50 and architecture.md:794 to match :893. Add `policy.rs::a_confident_person_card_never_asks_claude` and `focus_never_spends`.

findings.title: Nothing brings the implementer's diff back: collect has no trigger, no pane key and a permission prompt
findings.claim: After the implementer finishes, the mod runs `handoff report`. The hand-off then sits in `reported` until someone runs `handoff collect`. No document says the mod or a duty runs collect. The pane has `h` (hand off) and `g` (merge) but no collect key. On the chat side, collect lives in the deferred `room_handoff` tool behind the normal permission flow. So the review diff doesn't 'come back': the person has to know to ask for it, or approve a permission prompt for a deterministic step that isn't their decision.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1054 ('On the agent's turn.complete, the mod runs planroom handoff report KEY'); architecture.md:1068-1072 (`reported --> reviewing: handoff collect builds the proposed-change diff`; merge only from reviewing); architecture.md:1211 (list keys: `h` hand off, `g` merge, no collect); architecture.md:1225 (`room_handoff`: deferred, 'the normal permission flow'). KICKOFF R8: 'Its result comes back as a diff for review'; S4 step 3; S9 (tier B): 'every main flow can be driven from the mod ... at most two keystrokes'; principle 1.
findings.failure_scenario: In the S9 evidence run, the real implementer finishes and the pane shows the hand-off as reported, with no diff and no card. Pressing `g` fails because the state isn't reviewing, or it merges without review if the state check is loose. The person has to ask Claude to collect, and approve a tool search plus a permission prompt. The 'two keystrokes from pane focus' count fails for the hand-off flow, and the review isn't presented to the person.
findings.proposed_fix: Have the mod run `handoff collect KEY` right after `handoff report`, as a system or agent step in the same handler (it's deterministic and compensated by cancel). Deal one review card, 'worker-status-via-api: rules 2/2 met, +41 −12 in 3 files. Merge / Ask for changes / Cancel', with merge as a deliberate second key per DR-54. Add `agents.test.ts::report_then_collect_deals_the_review_card` and include the step in S9's key count.

findings.title: For the sole user, every phone edit and pick needs a second confirmation at the desk, and CI tests only a non-owner viewer
findings.claim: Rows under the owner's uid never apply. They become one card that the person confirms locally, and every remote `decide` waits for that confirmation too. KICKOFF says there is one user, so in practice every remote action is the owner's: a tap on the phone does nothing until the person is back at Claude Code and confirms a second card. The S11 CI path gets an 'attributed person edit' only by using a non-owner viewer (`u_test is not the owner`). The case that will actually happen, the owner on a phone, is tested only as becoming a card, and once confirmed its attribution is never specified.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1289 ('A row under the owner's own uid ... applies nothing ... one card the local person confirms'); architecture.md:1295 ('the next sync folds the pick into the one confirming card above, and live/head shows it as waiting'); contracts.md:871; feature_list.json S11 asserts ('u_test is not the owner; the owner's row and the decide row apply nothing and become one confirming card'); KICKOFF line 8 ('I'm the only user'); KICKOFF S11 ('An edit made there comes back as an attributed user edit'); KICKOFF principle 1 ('one tap to confirm'); S13 ('decision cards take one tap').
findings.failure_scenario: The owner, on a phone where localhost isn't reachable (the stated reason for remote mode), taps three Jev-pre-selected cards and renames a block. Nothing applies, and live/head shows all four as waiting. Hours later at the desk, the pane deals 'Apply 3 edits and 1 pick from your phone?'. The decisions cost two interactions on two devices and stayed stale in between, and S11's evidence run either shows a card instead of 'an attributed user edit' or attributes the result to `person:<os-user>`, not the phone.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a one-time device pairing the model can't see. The pane, or `planroom open`'s canvas, shows a short pairing code drawn only on the surface (never in tool output or in `/room` text). The owner enters it once on the Artifact page, which keeps it in localStorage and signs each inbox row with HMAC(key, docId‖body). Import applies a signed owner row as `person:artifact:<uid>` directly. Unsigned owner rows keep today's one confirming card. Specify the attribution of confirmed rows. Add an S11 CI case for the owner, signed and unsigned. Record it as an amendment to DR-52 with the threat model, which stays a guardrail as SECURITY.md already says.

findings.title: Accepting a batch can accept items added after the person saw it
findings.claim: Prefill batches per kind and person-stakes batches per kind grow as duty runs add items. A ghost batch per cause grows while its chat turn is still running. `decide CARD accept` or the pane's `a` key accepts 'the batch', and no document says it is bounded to the items visible at the card's `base`. Base compare-and-set protects fields, not batch membership, so items added between render and press get accepted unseen.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:790-791 ('one collapsed batch per kind'; 'Cards of one kind batch into one card'); architecture.md:896 (batch by cause, 'Accept 5 proposals?'); architecture.md:1205 (`a` accept the batch); contracts.md:493 (`batch: Option<BatchInfo>` with 'count and item handles'). KICKOFF R5: 'nothing the AI invents counts until a person accepts it'.
findings.failure_scenario: The pane shows 'Accept 5 proposals?' while the chat turn is still emitting ghosts. The person presses `a`, and by commit time the cause holds 7. All 7 are accepted, including 2 items the person never saw, which then count in lint and reconciliation.
findings.proposed_fix: Have batch accept take the card's `base` (or the item handles it rendered) and accept only those items. Later items stay ghosts, and a new card for them appears. Add `policy.rs::batch_accept_is_bounded_by_base`.

findings.title: consent_required tells agents to retry later, though only a person can clear it
findings.claim: `consent_required` has retry class `later` (and no `retry_after_ms`), but nothing an agent can wait for will clear it: only a person's pick on the consent card does. The same is true of the person-gated `person_required`, which correctly says `never` and names a card. With `later`, an agent re-polls on a timer and spends tokens.
findings.evidence: contracts.md:163 (`consent_required | permission | 5 | later | ... | provider, card`) vs contracts.md:162 (`person_required ... never ... card`); contracts.md:106-107 (`Later` with `retry_after_ms`). KICKOFF principle 2 (stable error codes, token-efficient outputs).
findings.failure_scenario: An agent running `intent next` gets `consent_required, retry: later` and retries every turn or on a backoff loop, each time paying the tool call and the reply, while the consent card sits unseen in the pane.
findings.proposed_fix: Set `consent_required` to retry `never`, with `details.card` and a hint that names the person action, mirroring `person_required`. Add a registry rule: a code whose clearing needs a person can't be `now` or `later`, enforced in `the_documented_error_table_is_the_error_codes`.

findings.title: Every envelope carries about 90 tokens of empty meta fields
findings.claim: `Meta` always serializes `took_ms`, `size`, `next`, `truncated`, `replayed`, `replayed_from`, `stale_repos`, `warnings`, the full `models` usage with both providers, and `model_requests`, even when they're empty or zero. The documented examples spend about 350 of 2,210 bytes on boilerplate. For the small-budget commands (`edit` and `review` at 400 tokens, `find` and `claim` at 600), that's 15 to 22% of the budget, and CLI agents pay it on every call.
findings.evidence: contracts.md:89-101 (Meta fields, none skip-if-empty); contracts.md:128-130 and 139-141 (examples); architecture.md:1139, 1145, 1135 (budgets 400 and 600). KICKOFF principle 2: 'Token-efficient by design ... every agent-facing output has a size budget'.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent doing a 20-step S4 regroup and intended change over the CLI spends about 1,800 tokens on `"replayed_from":null,"stale_repos":[],"models":{"jev":{"calls":0,...}}` that carry no information, and that baseline is what gets ratcheted into budgets.json.
findings.proposed_fix: Use `skip_serializing_if` for default or empty meta fields (schema defaults keep readers typed), drop `models` when both call counts are 0, and re-baseline budgets.json downward. Keep `seq` and `size` always present.

findings.title: A stray digit at the empty prompt can start a model call that spends money and can't be undone
findings.claim: DR-54 limits the band's buttons, which a bare digit presses, to leaves that aren't NotUndoable and aren't Handoff-class. But `intent next` (a capable-tier Claude call, about $0.15) and `decide --run` (Jev) are Edit-class, so they qualify. The ghosts they write can be undone. The spend can't, and neither can sending repo excerpts to a provider.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1216 ('A bare digit at the empty prompt presses it, so a stray digit at the start of a message must never do harm ... name only commands whose undo class isn't NotUndoable and whose permission class isn't handoff'); architecture.md:1120 (`intent next`, `decide --run` are Edit-class); architecture.md:940 (S03 stage call about $0.15). KICKOFF principle 1: 'Everything is reversible, which is what makes bold defaults safe'.
findings.failure_scenario: The band's next action is 'Draft the outcome stage' (`intent next`). The person starts a message with '1. retries should...' at the empty prompt, which presses the band and fires a capable-tier Claude call they didn't ask for. Six such slips in a session cost about $0.90, and the typed digit is swallowed.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a `spends` flag to CommandSpec, generated from the leaves that can make a model call. Band buttons and `PaneModel.next` may name a spending leaf only as a label that opens its card (like hand-off), or only when the decision cache can answer the call. Extend `packs.rs::a_suggestion_cannot_name_an_irreversible_command` and `keys.test.tsx::band_next_is_undoable` to cover spend.

verdicts.reason: Every place the tool result is defined names `result` and `meta.next` (contracts adds seq and warnings). None mentions `error`, and contracts makes `result` and `error` mutually exclusive Options. An error envelope therefore reaches the agent with no code, retry class, hint or details. I found nothing elsewhere that covers it: decisions.md and the tool-result budget test say nothing about error envelopes. S14 (tier A) depends on agents driving S1 and S2 through the tools, and principle 2 asks for stable error codes there.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:1227 'return the envelope's `result` and `meta.next`'; architecture.md:1518 (A-4) 'returns `JSON.stringify` of the envelope's `result` and `meta.next` as one string'; contracts.md:792 'the envelope's `result` plus `meta.next`, `meta.seq` and warnings'; contracts.md:83-84 `result: Option<T>` and `error: Option<ErrorObject>`, both skip_serializing_if none; architecture.md:922 says only that tools.test.ts serializes each tool result from the goldens, not that errors are included.

verdicts.reason: Redaction is applied to the whole tool output, with no field scope and no exemption for IDs, cursors or hashes. The docs never define the high-entropy threshold. Commit SHAs, uuid v7 event IDs and opaque cursors would plausibly trip a typical entropy detector, and no test checks that handles survive redaction. Whether IDs actually break depends on a threshold the design leaves open, so I uphold it as a real risk to S14's tools-only path.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:881 '`kernel::redact` runs on every Jev state, every Claude prompt, every session-backend request file and every mod tool output. It masks ... high-entropy strings'; contracts.md:792 'as compact JSON, after `kernel::redact`'; architecture.md:1302 repeats it, and its tests (`a_planted_repo_secret_reaches_no_request_or_tool_output`) check only that secrets are masked, never that handles survive.

verdicts.reason: Plan items can only be proposed with `intent propose --file F` (and `edit propose --file`). The tool input is a list of string arguments with no inline payload, so the chat model has to Write a file first. The guard denies Write under `.planroom/`, so the file lands somewhere else, and in default mode every Write prompts the person. That adds an interruption that isn't a person's decision to S3 (tier A), against principle 1.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:976 'it proposes items itself through `room_change` (ghosts, one batch per turn)'; architecture.md:1138 '`intent ... propose --file F`'; contracts.md:783 '"args": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } }'; architecture.md:401 'Edit, Write, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit under `.planroom/`' are denied; architecture.md:1106 the curator 'submits a reworded draft with `edit propose --file`' with tools `Read, Bash, Grep, Glob` (1231). No inline-payload or stdin form appears in any document.

verdicts.reason: The design says pending edits survive a reload in sessionStorage, but a reloaded tab has lost its in-memory bearer token. The only way back in is `e` or `/room open`, which opens the URL in the browser as a new tab, and a new tab starts with empty sessionStorage. The old tab keeps the edits but can't send them. Nothing defines what an unauthorized tab shows, and the empty-state audit covers only empty-workspace views. The window is narrow (edits are pending only while a request is in flight or `serve` is down, for example after a drain on upgrade), but the documented recovery doesn't work. That breaks principle 1's 'never lose what someone did'.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:1256 'Pending edits survive a reload in `sessionStorage` ... until confirmed'; architecture.md:1173 'which the tab keeps in memory ... A reload asks for a new code: `e` or `/room open`'; architecture.md:1172 'It opens `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/#code=...` in the browser itself'; architecture.md:1158 binds `127.0.0.1:0`; architecture.md:156 exits after 30 min with no client or on drain; architecture.md:1274 `empty_state_audit` 'visits every canvas view on an empty workspace'.

verdicts.reason: DR-60 removed the first-load card, but feature_list.json and DR-48's consequences still depend on it. That includes a tier A S7 CI step that keeps a card that will no longer exist. `Command::PersonInit`, which DR-60 says contracts gain, appears nowhere in contracts.md or the architecture's leaf and undo tables. The setup card is dealt 'when no backend is configured', and no document says whether strict replay counts as configured, so S7's max_cards 1 is at risk.
verdicts.evidence: decisions.md:1157 'A pack that a person lists in config or `PLANROOM_PACKS` loads with no card'; decisions.md:1159 'contracts gain `Command::PersonInit`' (grep finds PersonInit only in decisions.md); decisions.md:861 'the Ruby pack's first-load card is dealt on every fixture; S7's warm phase keeps it before the rescan'; feature_list.json S7 step 'planroom decide CARD keep --base SEQ --json (person) for the Ruby pack's first-load card'; the S1 assert 'the Ruby pack's first-load card among them'; architecture.md:958 the setup card for 'a workspace with none' (no backend); the fixture_note says only that 'strict replay counts as consent', not that it counts as a configured backend.

verdicts.reason: The Escalation bullet, the loop diagram and DR-50 all ask Claude for a person card when it reaches the top of the stack, with no band condition. The Policy bands section limits 'Ask Claude' to the escalate band, run lazily. The docs contradict each other, and neither says which process makes the call or whether a read triggers it.
